objective: Measure how much of the CBFS velocity error an eddy-viscosity-form correction can absorb on its own, by propagating the frozen extraction with the residual anisotropy term switched off and again with it on, and set the fraction beside the 70.5 to 92.1 percent Dow measured
rationale: Dow's structural-uncertainty method rests on one premise: that most of the RANS to truth velocity discrepancy can be represented as eddy-viscosity discrepancy. He measured that premise on eight random separated channel geometries and got 70.5 to 92.1 percent of the discrepancy norm, read from his Table 4.2 and checked here by arithmetic after two of its cells were found damaged by the scan. This lab has never measured its own equivalent on any case, and it now needs to, because the beta inversion on CBFS plateaued at about 0.09 percent of its data term against a 30 percent bar with a gradient verified against finite differences to better than 0.2 percent on four cells. A verified gradient and a flat objective point at what the optimizer is allowed to change rather than at the machinery, and the parameterization is the suspect: Dow infers the eddy viscosity itself, which enters the momentum equation directly, while beta multiplies a source term of the omega equation whose solution then has to produce the eddy viscosity through a transport operator, and wherever the stress limiter binds the eddy viscosity has no algebraic dependence on omega at all. This proposal tests the premise without touching the adjoint, because the frozen extraction already built for the sparse-regression rung produces exactly the decomposition needed: it converged on CBFS in 295 iterations at 6.2 s of CPU and outputs both the deficit term and the residual anisotropy that no eddy viscosity of any magnitude can represent. Propagating with the anisotropy term scaled to zero isolates the eddy-viscosity-form part; propagating with it on is the full correction and is already run. The verified sign conventions from the same work are reused unchanged, including the measured ratios that convicted each flipped sign. Both arms restart from the shipped baseline, as the source method specifies. Both cases involved are benchmark training cases and no scored test case is opened.
gate: Pre-registered before either arm runs: the absorption fraction is reported as a ratio of velocity error norms, in the same power as the number it is compared against, with the arithmetic printed rather than asserted. G1, the anisotropy-off arm is converged by the same settle criterion the frozen work used, not by an iteration cap. G2, the reference field's under-resolved top-wall strip is excluded from every error norm and the excluded cell count is stated. G3, the two arms differ in exactly one scale factor and nothing else. A fraction is reported with the region it was measured over, and no fraction is reported at all if either arm fails its settle criterion
cost_basis: measured: the frozen propagation on this case ran 15,000 iterations from the baseline at 16.8 core-min, and this item is two such propagations differing in one scale factor. The frozen extraction itself is 6.2 s of CPU on this case and is already done. The error norms and the fraction are arithmetic on written fields at no solver cost
expected_knowledge_gain: Three distinguishable outcomes and each one changes the next decision. If the eddy-viscosity-form part alone absorbs a fraction inside the band the source measured on separated flows, the premise under the whole uncertainty program holds on our case, and the beta parameterization is what stands between the lab and it, which makes a direct eddy-viscosity inversion worth pricing. If it absorbs far less while the full correction absorbs much more, the premise fails on this case, the residual anisotropy is the dominant error, and no richer scalar inversion would have rescued the plateau, which retires a line of work cheaply. If neither arm absorbs much, the finding is about the reference data or the propagation rather than about either method, and the band program stops before anything is sampled
